Generates the contaminated datasets for simulation study 2 (manuscript Figures 6, 7 and S.4–S.9).
Output: `simulation_data.parquet`, which is read by `1.1.2_Simulation_Fitting.Rmd`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(vsgoftest)
library(gamlss)
library(arrow)
library(rrobot)   
```

## Settings

The paper uses `nsim = 1000` with all distributions and contamination levels.
This file shows how the data were generated; rerunning it will not reproduce the exact `simulation_data.parquet` used in the paper, which is provided and read by the later files.
For a smaller run, lower `nsim` or shorten `distributions` / `percentages`.

```{r}
data_dir <- "data"

nsim          <- 1000
distributions <- c("df_T", "df_laplace", "df_normal", "df_gamma", "df_chisq", "df_weibull")
percentages   <- c("1%", "5%", "10%", "20%", "30%")

n          <- 500
perc_out   <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3)
n_out      <- round(n * perc_out)
thresholds <- seq(0.5, 0.6, by = 0.05)   # iForest score thresholds
```

## Distributions

```{r}
draw_data <- function(n) {
  list(
    df_T       = rt(n, df = 4),
    df_laplace = vsgoftest::rlaplace(n, mu = 0, b = 3),
    df_normal  = rnorm(n, mean = 10, sd = 3),
    df_gamma   = rgamma(n, shape = 2, scale = 1),
    df_chisq   = rchisq(n, df = 3),
    df_weibull = rweibull(n, shape = 1, scale = 3)
  )
}
```

## SHASH parameters of each distribution

Fitted once to 100,000 draws (Table 3). Used to place the outliers on the original scale.

```{r}
set.seed(123)

n_shash   <- 100000
fit_order <- c("df_normal", "df_T", "df_laplace", "df_gamma", "df_chisq", "df_weibull")

big_draws <- map(fit_order, function(d) {
  switch(d,
         df_normal  = rnorm(n_shash, 10, 3),
         df_T       = rt(n_shash, df = 4),
         df_laplace = vsgoftest::rlaplace(n_shash, mu = 0, b = 3),
         df_gamma   = rgamma(n_shash, shape = 2, scale = 1),
         df_chisq   = rchisq(n_shash, df = 3),
         df_weibull = rweibull(n_shash, shape = 1, scale = 3))
})

param_df <- map2_dfr(fit_order, big_draws, function(d, x) {
  fit <- gamlssML(x ~ 1, family = "SHASHo2", maxit = 10000)
  est <- coefAll(fit)
  tibble(dist = d, mu = est$mu, sigma = est$sigma, nu = est$nu, tau = est$tau)
})
param_df
```

## Contamination

Outlier magnitudes are chi-square(4)/5 + 3 on the z-scale, given a random sign for the symmetric distributions, and mapped back to the original scale with the SHASH parameters above.
For the normal distribution the z-scale is just (x - 10)/3.

```{r}
generate_sim <- function(sim) {
  dat <- draw_data(n)

  map_dfr(names(dat), function(dist_name) {
    x <- dat[[dist_name]]
    est <- param_df %>% filter(dist == dist_name)

    map_dfr(seq_along(n_out), function(j) {
      idx      <- sample(seq(n), n_out[j])
      out_vals <- rchisq(n_out[j], df = 4) / 5 + 3

      if (dist_name %in% c("df_T", "df_laplace", "df_normal")) {
        out_vals <- sample(c(-1, 1), n_out[j], replace = TRUE) * out_vals
      }

      x_out <- x
      if (dist_name == "df_normal") {
        z <- (x - 10) / 3
        z[idx] <- out_vals
        x_out <- 10 + 3 * z
      } else {
        x_out[idx] <- rrobot::normal_to_SHASH(out_vals, mu = est$mu, sigma = est$sigma,
                                              nu = est$nu, tau = est$tau)
      }

      map_dfr(thresholds, function(thr) {
        tibble(
          simulation             = sim,
          distribution           = dist_name,
          threshold              = thr,
          percentage             = paste0(perc_out[j] * 100, "%"),
          original_values        = list(x),
          outlier_infused_values = list(x_out),
          true_outliers          = list(seq(n) %in% idx)
        )
      })
    })
  })
}
```

## Run and save

```{r}
set.seed(42)

df_results <- map_dfr(seq_len(nsim), generate_sim) %>%
  filter(distribution %in% distributions, percentage %in% percentages) %>%
  mutate(percentage = factor(percentage, levels = c("1%", "5%", "10%", "20%", "30%")))

write_parquet(df_results, file.path(data_dir, "rawdata_simulations.parquet"))
df_results
```
